questions.1: A craft studio handles three workshop registrations. The three workshop registrations are independent. Each is either kept or cancelled, two mutually exclusive and exhaustive outcomes. The keep probabilities for workshop registrations 1, 2 and 3 are 0.5, 0.3, 0.7, respectively. Each kept registration contributes 9 USD and each cancellation contributes no money. A fixed setup cost of 6 USD is then deducted once from the combined contribution. There are no other receipts or costs. Record the net contribution for the three workshop registrations.
questions.2: A neighbourhood centre receives one rebate from each of two utility providers. The utility providers award payments independently. Each has exactly three mutually exclusive possible outcomes: no payment, a 3 USD payment, or an 8 USD payment. For the first provider these probabilities are 0.1, 0.8, 0.1, respectively. For the second provider they are 0.1, 0.15, 0.75, respectively. Add both payments; there are no other adjustments. Record the total payment, keeping first-provider then second-provider order.
questions.3: A museum issues one audio guide under exactly one of eight exhaustive, mutually exclusive visitor categories: Members, Children, Students, Seniors, Visitors, Teachers, Groups or Guests. Their probabilities are 0.05, 0.2, 0.2, 0.05, 0.1, 0.15, 0.2, 0.05, respectively. The corresponding fixed charges are 0, 0, 4, 4, 9, 9, 18, 18 USD, respectively. No other charges apply. Record the charge for this transaction.
questions.4: A community sports fund classifies one assistance application in exactly one of eight exhaustive, mutually exclusive categories: No assistance, Advice, Training, Practice, Equipment, Travel, Voucher or Cash. These eight named categories are the distinct outcomes in the sample space. Their probabilities are 0.04, 0.06, 0.08, 0.12, 0.23, 0.27, 0.11, 0.09, respectively; do not assume equal likelihood. The corresponding payouts are 0, 0, 8, 8, 19, 19, 29, 29 USD, respectively. Count the voucher at its face value as a payout. Each payout is fixed for its category, and no additional payments apply. Record the payout for one case.
questions.5: For one enrolment, an online course provider records exactly one of seven distinct, mutually exclusive and exhaustive service-resolution outcomes: A (course accessed on time); B (access reset requested); C (short access delay); D (duplicate charge corrected); E (alternative course accepted); F (later session accepted); G (course withdrawn by provider). These named outcomes form the sample space. Outcomes A and B award 0 USD service credit; C and D award 9 USD; E, F and G award 16 USD. Thus seven outcomes map to three possible credit values. B is 3 times as likely as A; C is 2 times as likely as A; D is 3 times as likely as B; E is as likely as B; F is 3 times as likely as E; G is as likely as F. There are no other payments or adjustments. Determine the outcome probabilities from these likelihood relationships and record the service credit.
questions.6: A community garden fundraiser has 13 physically distinct prize vouchers: 4 worth 0 USD each, 7 worth 4 USD each and 2 worth 10 USD each. Choose a subset of three uniformly without replacement, so every subset of three physically distinct items has the same chance. Ignore selection order. First add the face values. Then add one bonus of 6 USD if the selected subset contains at least one 4 USD item and at least one 10 USD item; otherwise add no bonus. Finally, if this adjusted amount exceeds 22 USD, pay only 22 USD; otherwise pay the adjusted amount. No other payments or deductions apply. Record the final payout.

task_c.1: Calculate and interpret the probability that the net contribution is exactly 12 USD.
task_c.2: Calculate and interpret the probability that the total payment is exactly 11 USD.
task_c.3: Calculate and interpret (i) the probability that the charge is less than 9 USD and (ii) the probability that it is at least 18 USD.
task_c.4: Calculate and interpret (i) the probability that the payout is less than 8 USD and (ii) the probability that it is at least 19 USD.
task_c.5: Calculate and interpret (i) the probability that the service credit is less than 9 USD and (ii) the probability that it is at least 16 USD.
task_c.6: Calculate and interpret (i) the probability that the final payout is less than 10 USD and (ii) the probability that it is at least 20 USD.
